features.name: Library scanning and automatic indexing
steps: Configure "included folders"
Choose the formats allowed for indexing, such as EPUB/PDF/FB2/MOBI/DJVU/DOC
Refresh
Scan the real file system and create Library entries
After adding files they appear on refresh
After deleting the file it disappears on refresh
After changing the scan directories or the format whitelist the library is recomputed. The official app explicitly supports user-specified scan directories and file types. Librera
features.expected: The library must be generated by scanning the real file system and include only whitelisted formats; after adding or deleting files the refreshed results change in sync; after changing the scan directories it is recomputed without leaving stale entries.

features.name: Multi-format document recognition and reading
steps: The same library contains EPUB, PDF, FB2, MOBI/AZW, DjVu, TXT, RTF, DOC/DOCX, ZIP, etc.
Each file type is correctly recognized for format and basic metadata
Tapping opens the corresponding reader
After returning to the Library the original file's identity and state are preserved. The official documentation lists these main supported formats. F-Droid
features.expected: Each format must be correctly recognized and opened with the corresponding reader, with metadata as consistent with the actual file as possible; after returning to the Library the original file's identity and state stay unchanged; a corrupted file must not cause a crash.

features.name: Library search and query state
steps: Enter conditions such as title, author, and extension in the Library
The list shows only matching items
Tapping the author further locates works by the same author
Clearing the search restores the full library
Searching must not copy or modify the original Book data. The official Library guide explicitly supports searching and finding by extension and author. Librera
features.expected: Search results must match the actual library data with title, author, and extension conditions all taking effect; clearing the query restores the full library; searching is read-only and must not copy or modify Book data.

features.name: Sorting, layout, and metadata views
steps: Switch between time/name and other sorts
Then toggle ascending/descending again
Choose a layout such as list, compact list, grid, or cover
Further organize the library by author, series, keyword, language, tag, publisher, publication date, etc.
All views point to the same set of Book data
features.expected: Sorting and layout only change the presentation and all views must point to the same set of Book data; ascending and descending are strictly reversed; when organizing by metadata such as author and tags the grouping is computed from the actual file metadata; the configuration persists.

features.name: Folder browsing and "folder as book"
steps: Enter a real storage directory from the "Folders" page
Create/enter a folder
Browse the readable files inside
Open an image directory as a book
The directory content order forms the reading order
After returning it is still in the correct directory context. The official app explicitly supports an in-app file browser and "opening an image folder as a book". GitHub
features.expected: The file browser must correspond to real storage paths; "folder as book" must form a reading sequence in the order of the files in the directory; after returning it is still in the correct directory context.

features.name: Library membership and real file operations
steps: Use "remove from library" on a book
The Library no longer indexes it but the original file continues to exist; it can be re-added after a rescan
Using "copy" produces a new file
"Move" changes the path
Only "Delete" deletes the actual file
The folder page and the Library reflect the changes in sync
features.expected: "Remove from library" only deletes the index without deleting the file, and a rescan can re-add it; copy, move, and delete must act on the real file system; after an operation the library and folder pages reflect the change in sync.

features.name: Recent and reading-progress persistence
steps: Open Book A
Read to the middle position
Exit
A appears in "Recent" with progress
After opening Book B the Recent order changes
Reopening A restores the original position
They continue to be preserved after restarting the app. The official documentation explicitly treats Recent and reading progress as core state. Librera
features.expected: Recent must be sorted by open time and show the real reading progress; reopening must return to the original position; the progress stays consistent between Recent and Library; it continues after a restart.

features.name: Reading-progress reset and cross-page sync
steps: The book already has reading progress
Use "reset progress" from the book menu
The progress indicator in Recent/Library resets to zero
Reopening enters from the starting position
The book file, favorites, and tag relations are not deleted because of this
features.expected: Resetting progress only clears the reading position and must not delete files, favorites, or tags; the progress indicator in Recent and Library resets to zero in sync; opening again must start from the beginning.

features.name: Favorites lifecycle
steps: Tap the star in the Library to favorite A
A appears on the favorites page
A is still the same book in the Library and shows the favorite state
Unfavorite on the favorites page
The Library syncs the un-favorite
After Rename/Move the favorite still corresponds to the same book
features.expected: Favorites are a persistent state: the same book must be consistent between the Library and the favorites page; unfavoriting syncs in both directions; after renaming or moving the favorite relation still corresponds to the same book; it remains after a restart.

features.name: Custom tags and book lists
steps: Add the custom tag "Testing books" to Book A/B
The tag appears in the favorites/tag organization
Opening by that tag shows only A/B
After removing the tag from A the collection is recomputed

Deleting a tag should unbind it from all bound books rather than deleting those books. The official documentation clearly states that custom tags can form custom book lists and that deleting a tag removes it from all bound books. Librera
features.expected: Tags are a many-to-many relationship and the same book can belong to several tags; opening by tag must show only the bound books; deleting a tag only unbinds it and must not delete any book file; after removal the collection is recomputed.

features.name: Playlist relationships and order
steps: Add several Books to the "playlist" from the book menu
These books appear on the Playlist page
The same book still exists in Library/Favorites
After adjusting the Playlist order the consumption/reading order follows the new order
Removing from the Playlist does not delete the book file
features.expected: A playlist is a reference relationship: after adding, the book still remains in the Library and favorites; order adjustments must persist and affect the consumption or reading order; removing an entry must not delete the book file.

features.name: Bookmark lifecycle
steps: Read to a certain position
Add a Bookmark
The bookmark page appears and links to the corresponding book/position
Tapping the Bookmark deep-links to the correct page
The edited bookmark text/target position is preserved
Deleting a Bookmark only deletes that locator record. The official app also supports both normal and floating bookmarks. Librera
features.expected: A bookmark must be bound to the file and position and jump to the correct page when tapped; it is preserved after edits; deleting a bookmark only deletes that locator record without affecting the book file or other bookmarks.

features.name: Reading-mode switching and per-format presets
steps: Open the document
Switch between Scroll / Book / Musician modes
Scroll uses vertical scrolling, Book uses page turning, and Musician supports auto-scroll
Set a default mode for a format
Books of the same format opened afterwards automatically use that mode. The official app explicitly supports three modes and per-format default modes. Librera
features.expected: The three modes must produce actual differences, i.e. scrolling, page turning, and auto-scroll; the default mode set for a format must take effect and persist when that format is newly opened; switching modes must not lose the current reading position.

features.name: Reading navigation and the status bar
steps: Turn pages/scroll in the book
The current page or reading percentage keeps changing
The progress bar, remaining pages, and other information update in sync
After jumping to a chapter/page the state is recomputed
Exiting and re-entering restores the correct position; the visibility settings for the status bar and the bookmark ribbon only change the presentation without modifying the reading records. Librera
features.expected: The page number or reading percentage must update in real time with the position, with the progress bar and remaining pages in sync; after a jump it is recomputed; exiting and re-entering restores the correct position; visibility settings only change the presentation without modifying the reading records.

features.name: In-document search and text selection
steps: Search for a keyword in a document that supports a text layer
Get multiple hits and jump to each one
Long-press to select a word/paragraph
Adjust the selection range
Copy, bookmark, or trigger other local operations
The reading position is preserved after returning. The official app explicitly supports multi-word search and complex text selection. F-Droid
features.expected: The search must return real hits based on the text layer and locate each one; text selection must correspond precisely to the text range; after returning to reading the position is preserved; documents without a text layer should give feedback.

features.name: TTS reading linked to the reading position
steps: Open a book that supports text
Start TTS
Start reading from the current reading position
Pause/Resume preserves the position
After changing the speed/pitch subsequent reading uses the new settings
After a manual jump the TTS start point syncs
The normal reading progress is still preserved after exiting. The official documentation confirms that Librera supports configurable TTS and built-in media controls. Librera
features.expected: TTS must start reading from the current reading position; pausing and resuming must not lose the position; speed and pitch changes apply to subsequent reading; after a manual jump the reading start point syncs; after exiting, the normal reading progress is saved correctly.

features.name: PDF annotation and edit saving
steps: Open the PDF
Switch to a Scroll mode that supports editing
Add a highlight, underline, strikethrough, handwriting, or drawing
You can cancel when exiting with unsaved content
After confirming the save and reopening, the annotations are still visible
Choosing save-as produces a new file without overwriting the original. The official documentation states that PDF annotation supports these tools and save/rename output. Librera
features.expected: Annotations must be bound to the page coordinates and display at the correct position after saving and reopening; exiting without saving must not produce modifications; "save as" must create a new file without overwriting the original; highlights, underlines, handwriting, and other types can all be saved.

features.name: Configure profiles and reading preferences
steps: Create/switch between different configured profiles
Configure the theme, font, layout, reading mode, etc. separately
After switching, the UI and reading behavior change immediately
The current profile is still preserved after a restart
Reset Profile restores the configuration defaults without accidentally deleting key user data. The official app supports multiple profiles and resetting. Librera
features.expected: Profiles must isolate their own reading preferences and take effect immediately when switched; the current profile is preserved after a restart; Reset Profile only restores the configuration defaults and must not delete user data such as books, bookmarks, or progress.

features.name: Full configuration backup → import restore
steps: Favorites/tags, Bookmarks, reading progress, and app settings already exist
Export produces a backup ZIP
Modify these states
Import an old backup
Settings, Bookmarks, Reading Progress, and Tags are restored
The corresponding Book files are still provided by local storage. The official documentation explicitly lists these four kinds of backup data. Librera
features.expected: The backup must include four kinds of data: settings, bookmarks, reading progress, and tags; after importing, these states are fully restored and bookmarks and progress map back to the local books; a corrupted backup file must not damage existing data.

features.name: Library path migration
steps: The original books are in /storage/Books/... and already have progress/tags/bookmarks
Move the whole batch of books to a new directory or SD card in the file system
Run Migrate to map the old path to the new path
The Library re-associates the new file location

The original reading progress, Bookmarks, and tags keep pointing to the correct book rather than treating the file at the new path as a completely new book. The official migration feature explicitly works by replacing the path in the configuration. Librera
features.expected: The migration must re-associate the files by replacing the path in the configuration; after migrating, the reading progress, bookmarks, and tags still correspond to the same book; when the path does not exist the original record is kept or clearly marked invalid and must not point to another file by mistake.
